Bridgewell resilience-grant allocation constitution handbook — section 1

Purpose. The constitution turns private due-diligence facts into consistent forced-choice allocations. A strong public benefit case never cancels an eligibility duty.

Rules. Bridgewell resilience-grant allocation constitution:
1. A candidate is ineligible when an unresolved financial conflict is present.
2. A candidate is ineligible when an active contracting suspension is present.
3. A sensitive-infrastructure project is ineligible when its data host is foreign controlled.
4. A candidate is ineligible when substantiated delivery failures divided by completed projects exceeds 0.20.
5. SELECT the eligible candidate with the highest public benefit score.
At least one candidate must be selected. Public benefit, households served, and readiness never make an ineligible candidate eligible.

Worked case. In this section, the highest-benefit candidate has an unresolved conflict, so the next-highest eligible candidate is selected. The result follows because an unresolved financial conflict can compromise fair allocation. Benefit, households served, readiness, and public value rank candidates only after private eligibility is established.

Practice note. Officers should separate the private basis for an allocation from a short applicant-facing justification. A public justification may cite project, benefit, households, readiness, region, and cost, but the selected candidate must still follow the constitution. Section code B-001.
